setup: Bulk cobalt oxide anodes fade fast: low electronic conductivity and large volume change on cycling

steps.output: PCO is mesoporous: hysteretic type IV isotherm, pores mostly 5-7 nm
steps.output_short: PCO is mesoporous: hysteretic type IV isotherm, pores mostly 5-7 nm
steps.question: What does the evidence below show about the porosity and pore structure?
observations: N2 isotherm: adsorption/desorption hysteresis from P/P0 ~0.5 to 1.0, uptake ~110 cm3/g
Pore size distribution (inset) peaks at ~5.5 and ~6.9 nm, tail below 4 nm
SEM: agglomerated faceted particles (~250-500 nm) with open gaps; internal mesopores not resolved

panels.caption_span: SEM image of the as-prepared PCO

steps.output: Li/PCO keeps ~840-870 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C (initial reversible ~870) ; Na/PCO fades from ~870 (1st discharge) to ~70 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C
steps.output_short: Li/PCO keeps ~840-870 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C (initial reversible ~870)
steps.property: how the material performs in service
steps.question: Taking the pore structure you characterised in step 1 as given, what does the evidence below show about how the material performs in service?
steps.refers_to_previous: the pore structure you characterised in step 1
observations: Na 1st discharge reaches ~865 mAh/g (plateau ~0.15 V); 1st charge ~470; 40th cycle ~60 mAh/g
Li 1st discharge: long plateau ~1.05 V to ~1330 mAh/g; 1st charge ~870 mAh/g with plateau ~2.0 V
Li cycling: charge capacity ~870 (cycle 1) rising to ~1050 (cycle ~17) and back to ~840 at cycle 40; CE ~96%
Na cycling: discharge capacity drops from ~870 (cycle 1) to ~480 (cycle 2) and ~70 mAh/g by cycle 40
